ideas.title: Bhanu aur Bolte Pakshi (Bhanu and the Talking Birds)
ideas.hook: In the village of Chandanpur, 7-year-old Bhanu finds a glowing feather near an ancient temple that lets him speak with birds, leading him to uncover a lost traditional water conservation secret during a drought.
characters: Bhanu - A curious 7-year-old village boy who loves grandmother's mythological stories.
Mitthu - A wise old parrot who guards the village banyan tree.
Dadi - Bhanu's loving grandmother who shares traditional wisdom.
ideas.moral: Nature holds the answers to our problems if we listen to it with care and respect.

ideas.title: Mithi aur Mitti ka Diya (Mithi and the Clay Lamp)
ideas.hook: During a festival, young Mithi creates a small, simple clay lamp with pure affection to help her hardworking potter father, proving that sincere love lights up the world brighter than grand riches.
characters: Mithi - An 8-year-old kind daughter of a humble village potter.
Kaku - Mithi's hardworking father who crafts pottery with devotion.
Uluka - A gentle white owl who visits pure-hearted children at night.
ideas.moral: True value comes from sincerity and love, not material wealth.

ideas.title: Gopala aur Mayur ka Mukut (Gopala and the Peacock Crown)
ideas.hook: Gopala, a young shepherd boy, discovers a magical peacock feather that can heal injured animals, but he must choose between selling it to help his family or using it to protect the village cattle.
characters: Gopala - A compassionate 9-year-old shepherd boy who cares deeply for animals.
Gauri - Gopala's energetic calf who gets into playful trouble.
Somu Kaka - A wealthy, greedy village trader who wants the magic feather.
ideas.moral: Selflessness and duty towards others are far greater than greed and personal gain.

why: Mithi aur Mitti ka Diya is a deeply relatable, warm, and visually rich story for children aged 4-10. It carries a clear emotional heart, connects strongly to Indian village traditions, and teaches humility and love without feeling preachy.
